title: FRAGILE GIANTS: UNDERSTANDING THE SUSCEPTIBILITY OF MODELS TO SUBPOPULATION ATTACKS
measurement_description: The paper measures the susceptibility of machine learning models to subpopulation poisoning attacks, where an adversary manipulates training data to degrade performance on specific subpopulations. For its text dataset (CivilComments), it evaluates how easily models can be poisoned to misclassify toxic/nontoxic comments that mention specific religious identities.
findings: The study found that models with greater complexity are significantly more susceptible to subpopulation poisoning attacks. For religious subpopulations specifically, the impact varied disproportionately with model size for medium-sized subgroups; for example, BERT Tiny exhibited only 2% target damage on the 'nontoxic, buddhist' subgroup (size 314), whereas the larger BERT Medium model suffered an 82% target damage on the exact same subgroup.
